sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: Which grip configuration in Table Tennis involves wrapping the index finger and thumb around the handle, mimicking the act of writing?
questions.answer: B) Penhold Grip

questions.question_text: In a standard game of Volleyball, what is the maximum number of consecutive touches a team is allowed before the ball must be sent over the net?
questions.answer: B) Three

questions.question_text: Which Yoga asana involves standing on one leg while the other foot is placed on the inner thigh of the standing leg to improve focus and balance?
questions.answer: B) Vrksasana

questions.question_text: In Table Tennis, hitting the top portion of the ball with an upward brush motion creates which type of spin?
questions.answer: C) Topspin

questions.question_text: True or False: In Volleyball, the Libero is a specialized defensive player who is permitted to serve, block, and spike the ball from anywhere on the court.
questions.answer: False

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of a 'block' setup in Volleyball?
options: A) To set up an attack
B) To intercept an opponent's spiked ball at the net
C) To serve the ball legally
D) To receive a fast serve
questions.answer: B) To intercept an opponent's spiked ball at the net

questions.question_text: True or False: Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation) is a fixed sequence of 12 yoga postures performed continuously to synchronize breath with movement.
questions.answer: True

questions.question_text: The Shakehand grip in Table Tennis is generally considered more advantageous for which style of play?
options: B) Equal power generation on both forehand and backhand wings
questions.answer: B) Equal power generation on both forehand and backhand wings

questions.question_text: Which breathing technique in Yoga is commonly referred to as 'Alternate Nostril Breathing'?
questions.answer: C) Anulom Vilom

questions.question_text: In a volleyball rotation, players shift their positions in which specific direction on the court when regaining the serve?
questions.answer: B) Clockwise

questions.question_text: Describe the basic racket movement required to generate backspin (underspin) during a Table Tennis rally. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To generate backspin, the player's racket must slice downward and forward beneath the ball at an open angle, brushing the bottom half to create backward rotation.

questions.question_text: Explain the correct hand positioning and posture for 'setting' a volleyball overhead. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Fingers should be spread wide and relaxed above the forehead, forming a triangle with thumbs and index fingers to cushion and direct the ball upwards.

questions.question_text: State two therapeutic benefits of practicing Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose) on a regular basis. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Bhujangasana expands the chest, improving respiratory functions. It also stretches the abdominal muscles and strengthens the lower spine, which helps relieve mild postural backaches.

questions.question_text: What is the fundamental difference in finger placement between the Shakehand and Penhold grips in Table Tennis? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Shakehand grip involves grasping the handle with the lower three fingers while resting the index finger on the blade. The Penhold grip wraps the thumb and index finger around the handle.

questions.question_text: Define a defensive 'dig' in volleyball and state when it is most appropriately utilized. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A dig is a forearm pass made from a low posture, utilized primarily to receive and keep a hard-driven opponent's spike from hitting the floor.

questions.question_text: Explain how heavy topspin dynamics affect the trajectory, bounce, and opponent's return in a Table Tennis match. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Heavy topspin creates downward air pressure, causing the ball to dip quickly and bounce sharply forward on the table. If blocked incorrectly with a flat racket, the ball will aggressively kick upward and fly off the table.

questions.question_text: Detail the rotational system rules a volleyball team must strictly observe when winning the right to serve. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: When a receiving team wins a rally and the right to serve, all six players must rotate exactly one position clockwise. This shifting protocol ensures every player systematically alters their offensive and defensive court zones throughout the match.

questions.question_text: Describe the physical mechanics of Tadasana (Mountain Pose) and its core objective as a foundational yoga posture. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Stand with feet together, ground the toes firmly, tighten the thigh muscles, and lengthen the spine while lifting the chest. Its core objective is to establish perfect postural alignment and neuromuscular body awareness for more complex standing poses.

questions.question_text: Outline the key biomechanical steps an attacker must follow to execute a powerful volleyball smash (spike) at the net. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: An effective spike requires a coordinated approach run, an explosive two-footed upward jump, a mid-air arching of the back, and striking the ball at the highest possible point with a forceful, downward arm swing.

questions.question_text: Compare the importance of footwork and spatial stance in Table Tennis versus Volleyball, highlighting how alignment impacts defensive readiness and stroke/pass execution. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: In Table Tennis, a low, wide stance with rapid side-to-side micro-steps is vital for maintaining balance against fast spins and executing quick forehand loops. Conversely, Volleyball requires an athletic 'ready' posture with weight on the toes, enabling explosive dives or jumps for blocking and digging. Both sports demand immediate spatial adjustments to defend and transition to offense effectively.

questions.question_text: Analyze the therapeutic role of integrating Paschimottanasana and Kapalabhati Pranayama for an athlete aiming to enhance core endurance and lung capacity for net games. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Paschimottanasana deeply stretches the hamstrings and strengthens the lower back, providing athletes with the flexibility needed for low defensive digs. Meanwhile, Kapalabhati Pranayama consists of forceful exhalations that heavily condition the abdominal core and clear the respiratory tract. Together, they significantly boost the lung capacity and structural endurance necessary for prolonged, high-intensity rallies.
